newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's Kandla oil jetties closed to mid-Dec.
newsitem.headline: India's Kandla oil jetties closed to mid-Dec.

text.p: The two oil product receiving floating jetties at the Indian west coast port of Kandla are expected to stay closed until the middle of December, a source in Bombay said on Tuesday.
"It will take another two weeks or so before the jetties could be re-opened," the source, who is familiar with the situation, said.
The closure of the two jetties has led to a long queue of tankers waiting to discharge outside the port and waiting time has almost doubled, traders said.
According to the latest berthing schedule from the port, there are 30 liquid tankers anchored off the port, of which 15 are carrying diesel.
"The oil tankers that are at the top of the queue right now arrived sometime in October," one shipping source said.
The two jetties were closed on October 20-21 after a collision involving two tankers. Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd owns one jetty and state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) the other.
As a result of the closure, IOC has drastically reduced the number of diesel cargoes it imports through Kandla via monthly tenders.

In its January purchase tender, only two out of the six cargoes were to be delivered to either Kandla or Goa while in December only four out of the 13 cargoes purchased were to be delivered to either of the two ports.
This contrasted with its October and September purchases where all three and six cargoes awarded in each tender respectively, were for delivery to either Goa or Kandla.

The port also feeds the 1,443 km Haldia-Batinda pipeline which transports petroleum products to north India. The two floating jetties were commissioned early this year to ensure that pipeline operations were optimised.
The closure of the jetties has not affected the pipeline throughput due to the high stock level, the source said.
IOC cancelled its tender to buy diesel for November delivery in part due to port congestion, traders said.
The two floating jetties are capable of handling annually at least 1.5 million tonnes of petroleum product each, the source in Bombay said.
Oil demand in the area has not been affected by the closure of the jetties as "there has been a good inventory build up as the market is entering a peak demand period," the source said.
Kandla is India's biggest oil port and handled about eight million tonnes of petroleum products and 12.5 million tonnes of crude last year.
